statements.text: The Chinese government also uses artificial intelligence, AI, for the troves of data it collects on its own citizens every day, particularly on ethnic minorities like the Uighers, against whom the Chinese government is committing human rights abuses.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Senator Dick Durbin advocating for the U.S. Innovation and Competition Act (USICA), citing China's AI-enabled surveillance as a national security concern.

statements.text: But the basic question we face is whether or not the issue of AI is a quantitative change in technology or a qualitative change. The suggestions that I've heard from experts in the field suggest it's qualitative. Is AI fundamentally different? Is it a game changer? Is it so disruptive that we need to treat it differently than other forms of innovation?
statements.venue: Opening statement, Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing 'Oversight of A.I.: Rules for Artificial Intelligence'

statements.text: I think what's happening today in this hearing room is historic. I can't recall when we've had people representing large corporations or private sector entities come before us and plead with us to regulate them.
statements.venue: Questioning at Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman

statements.text: This explosive growth has been driven by advances in technology; namely, generative artificial intelligence. What used to take technological expertise and a lot of time can now be done with the push of a button. Countless apps can swap someone's face onto another person's body or can digitally remove someone's clothing so they appear to be nude.
statements.context: Senate floor speech by Dick Durbin advocating for passage of the DEFIANCE Act and related child-protection legislation.

statements.text: We are currently living with the results of our failure to regulate Big Tech when it came to social media. Let’s not make the same mistake when it comes to AI. This provision by Senator Cruz will allow Big Tech and bad actors to prey on the lack of regulations in the AI space and develop deceptive, biased, and potentially dangerous tools that hurt ordinary Americans and diminish trust in technology.
statements.venue: Senate floor speech on the reconciliation bill and the AI moratorium provision

statements.text: Should AI companies be able to use their materials freely as ``fair use'' or should they receive compensation when their works are used to train AI models?
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI companies' use of copyrighted works for model training.

statements.text: But the ultimate winner in this is going to be the AI because if they escape this responsibility, they can use Mr. Baldacci's product and make money off of it.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Committee hearing examining the AI industry's use of copyrighted works for AI training, featuring testimony from expert witnesses.

statements.text: Every time we get down to the nub of the question, can these giant corporations take the copyrighted work of individual citizens, we get distracted with, well, it is for the good of the country, maybe it is not so bad, we have an arms race on, there is an AI czar. [...] I think in America, we have rights. Those rights are what protect us. These rights are being violated. And if we are going to succeed as a nation and uphold our principles as a nation, we better darn well enforce the individual rights on which the nation is founded.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on the AI industry's use of copyrighted works for AI training, chaired by Senator Hawley questioning Professor Lee.

statements.text: We have all seen the headlines. Meta's own internal research showed harm to children on Instagram and in virtual reality spaces. AI and platforms like ChatGPT, Character.AI, and OpenAI are facing lawsuits for failing to prevent harmful, even deadly, conversations with minors.
statements.context: Senator Durbin speaks on the Senate floor advocating for the bipartisan STOP CSAM Act, which targets online child sexual exploitation by imposing liability and transparency requirements on technology platforms.

statements.text: I'm going to be working on some legislation I want to talk to Senator Hawley about to make sure AI companies are held accountable for the products they design and deploy. The AI LEAD Act would establish a Federal cause of action against AI companies for harms caused by their systems.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing examining harms of AI chatbots, featuring testimony from affected families.

statements.text: I believe whether you’re talking about CSAM or you’re talking about AI exploitation, the quickest way to solve the problem and to do it with a real determination, is to give to the victims a day in court. Believe me, as a former trial lawyer, that gets their attention in a hurry.
statements.venue: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI chatbot harms (press release)

statements.text: Congress finds the following: (1) Artificial intelligence systems are products that shift decision-making power and responsibility away from humans to software-based systems, often without direct human oversight. (2) These products, while holding great promise, have caused and will cause harm to businesses and individuals. For example, multiple teenagers have tragically died after being exploited by an artificial intelligence chatbot. [...] SEC. 101. DEVELOPER LIABILITY FOR HARM TO BUSINESS OR CONSUMER. (a) In General.—In any liability action, the developer shall be liable to a claimant if the claimant establishes by a preponderance of the evidence— (1) that— (A) the developer failed to exercise reasonable care with respect to the design of the covered product; and (B) the failure to exercise reasonable care was a proximate cause of harm to the claimant [...]
statements.context: Introductory statement by Senator Dick Durbin on the Senate floor requesting unanimous consent to print the full text of S. 2937, the AI LEAD Act, into the Congressional Record.

statements.text: This Act may be cited as the ``Aligning Incentives for Leadership, Excellence, and Advancement in Development Act'' or the ``AI LEAD Act''. [...] Congress finds the following: (1) Artificial intelligence systems are products that shift decision-making power and responsibility away from humans to software-based systems, often without direct human oversight. (2) These products, while holding great promise, have caused and will cause harm to businesses and individuals.
statements.context: Senator Durbin introduced S. 2937, the AI LEAD Act, on the Senate floor and asked unanimous consent to print the full bill text in the Record.

statements.text: Democrats and Republicans don’t agree on much these days, but we’ve struck a remarkable bipartisan note in protecting children online. Big Tech’s time to police itself is over. Kids and adults across the country are turning to AI chatbots for advice and information, but greedy tech companies have designed these products to protect their own bottom line—not users’ safety. By opening the courtroom and allowing victims to sue, our bill will force AI companies to develop their products with safety in mind. Our message to AI companies is clear: keep innovating, but do it responsibly.
statements.venue: Press release introducing the AI LEAD Act with Sen. Hawley

statements.text: With the push of a button, generative AI can swap someone's face onto another person's body, remove that person's clothing so they appear nude, or undress someone to show them in lingerie or other exposed positions.
statements.context: Senate floor statement by Dick Durbin (D-IL) requesting unanimous consent to pass the DEFIANCE Act.

statements.text: Far too many young people, especially women and girls, are living in agony every day knowing deepfake nudes of them are circulating on the Internet. They ought to be able to sue the perpetrators who are harming them, and it’s past time to open the courtroom to survivors. I thank OpenAI for acknowledging the gravity of the situation and supporting our bill. I encourage other AI companies to follow suit and for the House of Representatives to finally advance this key piece of legislation.
statements.venue: Press release on OpenAI endorsing the DEFIANCE Act
